title.narrative: Circle of Impact: Sustainable bamboo chain with biochar enabling sanitation for local communities

description.narrative: In rural Ghana, agricultural value chains face deep-rooted social and environmental sustainability challenges. High national inflation, seasonal income fluctuations, and climate shocks severely strain rural families, leaving an estimated 91% of farmers earning below a living income. Driven by poverty and a lack of formal oversight, an estimated 10.3% of children aged 5–17 years old engage in child labour. Furthermore, agricultural operations lack structured occupational health and safety (OHS) practices, while around 25 million people in Ghana lack access to safe sanitation, leading to significant soil and water pollution from untreated waste.Project BeneficiariesThe project directly targets over 6,900 local beneficiaries in the Volta Region:? 6,200+ Bamboo Farmers, Factory Workers, and Households: Gaining stabilised, fair-wage employment, safe working conditions, and agricultural support via local cooperative hubs.? 700+ Students: Benefiting from circular school dry-toilet facilities (waters, sanitation and hygiene (WaSH)), hygiene education, and reduced absenteeism — particularly for girls through menstrual health support.? Women in Local Communities: Gaining new paid management roles overseeing local WaSH and waste recycling operations.Envisioned ImpactThe project "Circle of Impact" establishes a fully integrated, circular bamboo-to-toilet value chain to deliver systemic change:? Socio-Economic: Increases farmer incomes (by an average of 59%) through transparent bamboo sourcing while mitigating child labour risks via community protection mechanisms and access to education.? Working Conditions: Standardises OHS, provides protective gear, and establishes structured grievance and gender-equality policies.? Environmental & Circularity: Diverts non-pulpable bamboo waste (approx. 20%) and collected human sanitation waste into biochar using a dedicated pyrolysis plant. Returned to farmers as an organic soil improver, this biochar replaces synthetic fertilisers, enhances crop yields, sequesters carbon, and unlocks additional revenue via certified carbon credits.
